title: Keya House Warm Line:
title_short: Keya House Warm Line · Somewhere You Can Call
headline: The warm line is a real person with lived experience who picks up and talks with you. Not a call center, not a crisis line.
story: A phone rings at Keya House and Madison picks up.
Amber explains: call and talk with a peer for up to 15 minutes about anything, and it doesn't always have to be a struggle. It is not a crisis line; for crisis there is 988.
A warm line is just a safe space to talk with a peer. The video ends on the ask MHA wants: if you're struggling, call this number.

Loops: L1 “Who picks up?” opens on the ringing phone at 0:00 and closes on “Keya House, this is Madison.” L2 “What is a warm line?” opens at 0:05 and closes on “a safe space to call and conversate with a peer” at 0:36. Stakes: someone who is struggling knows there is a real person to call.
do: Open on the ringing phone with “Someone will pick up.” on frame 1.
Cut to Madison's real calls over Amber's lines. Mute Madison's own sound under Amber.
Captions on every spoken line, in one place for the whole video.
Keep the 988 line and put it on the text card. 988 is on that card only.
End card: “If you're struggling, call this number.” + the Keya House warm-line number MHA confirms + MHA Nebraska, 5 s.
dont: Not therapy, diagnosis, treatment or crisis. Not a hotline, hospital or office.
No 988 on the end card. Never type a phone number from Google: use the number MHA confirms.
No guest face without a signed release. No street number on screen.
No desk, keyboard or paper filler B-roll.
